doc.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Boyhood singing idols Gene Austin and Russ Columbo
summary: He modeled his high tenor on Gene Austin and admired Russ Columbo's song choices.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah, it was really a lot of pretty stuff. I took after Gene Austin. I liked Gene Austin. He was on the radio every night for half an hour. He had a high tenor voice like I had. So I used to sing a lot of his songs.
When did you start listening to him? When did you recognize him?

I recognized him before anybody, because he was singing, and I was always interested in that. I also liked Russ Columbo. Russ Columbo was very handsome. Italian extraction, I think he was. He got killed in Los Angeles. He was a very handsome guy, good singer. He was, I thought, better than Bing Crosby, but his life got cut short.
What made you want to sing to emulate him?

I liked the songs that he chose. I used to sing a lot of the songs that he would sing. I heard Russ Columbo do [Hendricks sings:] “Alone from night to night you’ll find me too weak to break the chains that bind me. I need no shackles to remind me. I’m just a prisoner of love.” I love that song. To this day I love that song. That’s great song. He’s the first one I heard sing that, ever.
That’s beautiful. I can’t think of whom I remember singing that, but . . .
Billy Eckstine sang it. It’s a great song.
